rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE SAFETY MEASURES AND PENALTIES RELATIVE TO THE OPERATION OF MOTORCYCLES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11235, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MOTORCYCLE CRIME PREVENTION ACT”
rows.title_short: Rationalizing The Safety Measures And Penalties Relative To The Operation Of Motorcycles, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11235, Otherwise Known As The “ Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act ”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to balance the benefits derived from innocent motorcycle users with those who utilize the said vehicle to carry out crimes. 
Lowers the penalties for violation of RA No. 11235 or the Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act for failure to comply with the registration requirement and for driving a motorcycle without the required number plate.
Requires the owner or possessor of motorcycle whose number plate is lost, damaged, or stolen to report the same to the LTO and the PNP through the Joint PNP and LTO Operations and Control Center within seventy-two (72) hours from discovery of such fact, and request a replacement number plate or be penalized by not more than Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00). However, if the lost, damaged, or stolen number plate or readable number plate is used with an offense penalized under the Revised Penal Code or special laws, the failure of the owner to report within three (3) days the fact of the loss, destruction or theft, shall subject the owner to a fine of not more than Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000.00), among others.
Requires owners of motorcycles with number plates not in conformity with the provisions of this Act, to renew their registration and apply for the required readable number plate not later than June 30, 2025 and requires the LTO to produce, release, and issue the number plates as required by this Act until December 31, 2025.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE SYSTEM OF FILING OF DELAYED REGISTRATION OF BIRTHS IN THE COUNTRY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ACT NO. 3753
rows.abstract: Seeks to amend Act No. 3753 (the Law on Civil Registry Status) to establish a formal system for the delayed registration of births. It introduces stricter guidelines and procedures for verifying the legitimacy of late applications. The amendment mandates that birth registration must occur within thirty (30) days of birth but allows for late registration if specific conditions are met. Additionally, it proposes requiring extra documentation, field visits, and interviews by local civil registrars. A mandatory ten (10) day public notice period for all late registration applications will also be implemented. This proposal seeks to emphasize the importance of the Philippine Statistics Authority´s Negative Certification of Birth Records as a required document to enhance the integrity of the civil registry.

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING SOLIDARITY CONTRIBUTION ON THE MOST AFFLUENT FILIPINOS FOR THE BENEFIT OF PUBLIC HEALTH AND CLIMATE CHANGE RESILIENCY
rows.abstract: Proposes a solidarity contribution based on net worth as of December 31 each year, with corresponding rates outlined in a provided table.  Provides that a Solidarity Contribution Return be filed, which must include total assets, liabilities, and net worth. The amount payable will be divided into installments over several periods and specific dates. Furthermore, the assessment and collection of this contribution will follow the same procedures as those for income, estate, and donor´s taxes as specified in the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC). The revenues generated from this contribution will be allocated exclusively for the following purposes: a) Universal Health Care Act; health expenditures, including hospitals and medical facilities; education and training for medical students in public universities; additional doctors for public hospitals; Disaster Calamity Quick Response Funds; and financial support for local government units (LGUs) to assist evacuees displaced during climate disasters.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INCREASE FARM PRODUCTIVITY BY REDUCING LAND FRAGMENTATION
rows.abstract:
Aims to address land fragmentation, which has resulted in decreased agricultural productivity and ongoing poverty in the sector. Includes easing restrictions on farm sizes, removing limitations on agricultural land transactions, and promoting a dynamic rural land market.

Proposes the following: 

- Establishing a ceiling requirement for landholdings 
- Removing the need for Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) clearances for ownership transfers 
- Eliminating the requirement for approval of land conversion from agricultural to non-agricultural use, among others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ENHANCED BENEFITS, WELFARE, AND REINTEGRATION OF REPATRIATED FILIPINO MIGRANT WORKERS INTO THE PHILIPPINE ECONOMY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to help Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) find local entrepreneurial, educational, and employment opportunities should they choose to settle permanently in the Philippines. 

Provides returning OFWs with access to financial literacy training and seminars, as well as the necessary capital to start their own businesses once they decide to do so.

Proposes the following initiatives:
- Business-oriented capacity-building training
- A financing/loan program for OFW-owned micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs)
- Job fairs for civil service-qualified OFWs
- Assistance from the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
- Programs for qualified and highly skilled OFWs to teach in academic institutions, among others.

rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others as follows:  EARMARKED REVENUES - are identified revenues required by statute to be used for designated activities, benefits, or purposes, and must be accounted for separately from the government´s general revenues.Â  ONE FUND CONCEPT - means accrual of all income, fees, charges, assessments, and other receipts or revenues collected by gov´t offices/agencies to the General Fund of the NG and deposited in the National Treasury.Â  SPECIAL ACCOUNTS IN THE GENERAL FUND (SAGF) - the fund whereby proceeds of specific revenue measures and grants earmarked by law for specific priority projects are recorded.

Proposes that all earmarked revenues collected by any government . . . shall accrue to the General Fund of the National Government and shall be maintained as Special Accounts within the fund and may be temporarily utilized for other authorized expenditures under the GAA, provided that cash receipts from earmarked revenues are recorded as separate SAGFs and requires that any funds temporarily used for other authorized expenditures remain readily available to fulfill the eligible expenditures charged against the SAGFs when needed.

rows.title_short: Philippine Agriculturists Act
rows.abstract:

Provides for the examination, registration, and licensure of agricultural practitioners; the supervision, control, and regulation of the practice of the agriculture profession in the Philippines; the development and upgrading of the Bachelor of Science (BS) in Agriculture curriculum; the development of the professional competence of registered agriculturists through Continuing Professional Development (CPC); and integration of the agriculture profession through membership of registered agriculturists in an accredited integrated professional organization.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE NATIONAL ECONOMIC AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 230, SERIES OF 1987, AND AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, SERIES OF 1987, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Economy, Planning And Development Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reorganize and institutionalize the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) into the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDEV) which shall serve as the lead integrator of the country´s economic program and policies.
Establishes, operates and maintains a regional office in each region of the country, except the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
Attaches different agencies to the DEPDEV for purposes of administrative supervision, policy coordination and policy and program coordination, and the Public-Private Partnership Center of the Philippines (PPPC) for budgetary purposes and administrative supervision.
Establishes the Economy and Development Council (ED) headed by the President of the Philippines which shall serve as the executive collegial body responsible for directing and providing overall policy direction on economic matters. 
Establishes different Committees of the ED Council which shall be the main coordinating mechanism that ensures that the policy environment is conducive to promoting inclusive and sustainable growth.
Provides separation and retirement benefits for employees who are separated from the service as a result of the consolidation and reorganization of the NEDA.
